response_text: To understand the utility of PSP, the difference between PSP and MSP is that the MSP is used in kernel mode, while PSP is for user mode tasks. Therefore, for managing values in a thread stack PSP is essential as MSP deals with system-level operations. If PSP is not set to the stack pointer, then the PSP will be accessing invalid memory which can corrupt data and crash the code or cause a hardfault. If PSP is not initialised, garbage from previous operations can still be stored in the memory affecting the expected output. Since the stack pointer allows the code to iterate through the different register values, if PSP is not set to it, the values cannot be assigned to the memory address of the thread stack. This leads to an invalid thread stack that deviates from expected use as PSP helps to point to the top of the stack. The runFirstThread function relies on PSP to utilise the thread stack, so when it is called directly after the line to set PSP to the stack pointer, the code could also crash from that point.\n
